label: Figure 1
title: The Department's General Fund lines, FY2026 and FY2027
caption: Enacted General Fund appropriations to the Alabama Department of Mental Health by line, as printed in the Legislative Services Agency's comparison sheets for FY2026 and FY2027. Values are as published, not adjusted for inflation.
how_to_read: Each pair of bars is one line of the Department's General Fund budget, the left bar for FY2026 and the right for FY2027. The total line dwarfs the others, so switch it off in the legend to compare the programme lines. A missing bar means the line did not exist that year; a bar at zero means the line was kept and funded at nothing, as with the 988 call centers in FY2027.

explain.text: The General Fund is about one-sixth of the Department's revenue, but it pays for what Medicaid does not.
The line fell from $500,000 to zero in FY2027; opioid-settlement appropriations carried money for 988 in 2025 and 2026.

source: Extracted by the builder from the Legislative Services Agency's enacted comparison sheets for FY2026 and FY2027. Values are as published; each row of the data file names its reference.

label: Figure 2
title: Involuntary beds per 100,000 residents against the planning benchmark
caption: Alabama's involuntary (civil-commitment) bed capacity as the Department has reported it, beside the 30-per-100,000 minimum of the Treatment Advocacy Center that the Department uses as its planning benchmark.
how_to_read: Three bars: the count at the start of FY2025 (repeated in August 2025), the count as of 13 January 2026, and the benchmark. The gap between the second and third bars is the 779 beds the Department prices in its January 2026 presentation. The bars count beds the Department treats as available under commitment orders, which include contracted community-hospital beds and crisis residential beds.

explain.text: Thirty beds per 100,000 is a published minimum, not a law or a federal standard.

source: Extracted by the builder from the Department's annual report for FY2025 and its budget presentations of August 2025 and January 2026. Values are as published.

label: Figure 3
title: How the eight domains and four cross-sector systems depend on one another
caption: The report's cross-domain dependency map drawn as a graph. Each arrow is one row of the map: the domain at the tail conditions the domain at the head, and the row's Alabama evidence travels with the arrow.
how_to_read: Start from any circle. Arrows leaving it show what that part of the system sets the terms for; arrows arriving show what it depends on. Select an arrow to read the evidence the report gives for that link, with its sources. Select a circle to see the figures the report and its baseline tables hold for that domain. The arrows are the report's own reading of how the parts connect; the evidence on each arrow is sourced, the choice of arrows is not.

explain.text: Thirteen links, taken row for row from the report's dependency table. Nothing is added.

source: Drawn by the builder from the report's own cross-domain dependency table as revised on 3 October 2026. The drawing is the builder's; the links and their wording are the report's.

label: Figure 4
title: Alabama's rank among the 50 states and the District of Columbia, by measure
caption: Alabama's rank on each measure in Mental Health America's State of Mental Health in America 2025. Most of the underlying data were collected in 2022 and 2023.
how_to_read: A short bar is a good rank and a long bar a poor one. Read the measures in two groups: the prevalence measures, where Alabama sits in the better half, and the access measures, where it sits at or near 51st. Hover a bar for Alabama's value and the national value. A rank says where Alabama stands in the order, not how far it is from the next state.

explain.text: Ranks are of 51; rank 1 is best on every measure.

source: Extracted by the builder from Mental Health America's 2025 report and ranking tables. Values are as published.

label: Figure 5
title: Federal Uniform Reporting System measures, Alabama and the United States, 2025
caption: Measures from SAMHSA's Uniform Reporting System tables for Alabama. The 2025 reporting year runs from October 2024 to September 2025.
how_to_read: Each row is one measure, with Alabama beside the national figure and Alabama's own figure a year earlier. Check the label for whether a row covers all ages or adults only. The two readmission rows rest on one readmission among 68 discharges, so a change of a few people moves the percentage a long way.
